newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Metals- China copper concentrate prices weak.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals- China copper concentrate prices weak.

text.p: China's copper concentrate market remains soft, pressured by large concentrate stocks at major smelters and healthy domestic production, metal traders said on Monday.
"Chinese (smelters) bought too much concentrate last year. Most smelters have big inventories and domestic production of concentrate is quite good," said one China-based source.
The domestic price of copper concentrate currently ranges from under 13,000 yuan ($1,567) a tonne to about 15,000 yuan ($1,808), sources said.

He said the market had earlier been expecting China to buy copper, but with the current configuration of LME versus Shanghai Metal Exchange prices, he would rather import copper concentrate and refine it domestically.

Shanghai copper futures ended up on Friday on a technical rebound supported by sharp price falls on Thursday, with the most actively traded September 1997 contract ending at an intraday high of 23,430 yuan ($2,825), up 60 yuan.

China imported about 840,000 tonnes of copper concentrate in 1996, and is expected to import about the same amount this year. "But since copper production is increasing, in effect, they are importing less concentrate," one source noted.
An east China smelter contacted said demand for Chinese copper was soft in the Asia-Pacific region and that it was having trouble finding regional buyers for its July contracts.
"Nobody wants to buy copper for July and August, but we hope the situation will improve in September," said a smelter source. He quoted copper at $2,520 a tonne FOB China

In other base metals, some traders reported small amounts of aluminium buying from Japan on Monday against the weakening dollar. The dollar fell briefly as low as 111.80 yen in midday trade on renewed concerns about Japan's trade surplus.
In tin, a source at a major smelter in south China said that despite their recent jump, LME prices were still unattractive for exports, given that domestic tin cost the equivalent of $5,800 a tonne.
"Exports are still difficult, the price has to go up a bit more," the source said.
LME tin closed on Friday at $5,710 a tonne, rising to $5,720 a tonne in inter-office trade. ($1=8.294 yuan)
